vocabulary.meaning: a feeling that something good will happen in the future
examples: Many people begin a new year with hope.
He hopes the coming year will bring better opportunities.

vocabulary.meaning: a firm decision to do or change something, often at the start of a new year
examples: Her New Year's resolution was to exercise more.
It can be difficult to keep a resolution for twelve months.
Setting a clear goal can improve motivation.
One of his goals is to learn another language.

vocabulary.meaning: the belief that good things are likely to happen
examples: The new year created a sense of optimism.
Her optimism helped the team stay positive.

vocabulary.meaning: a belief about what will probably happen
examples: People had high expectations for the coming year.
Unrealistic expectations can lead to disappointment.

vocabulary.meaning: a strong desire to achieve something
examples: His ambition is to start his own company.
Ambition can encourage people to work hard.

vocabulary.meaning: a situation that makes it possible to do something useful or desirable
examples: A new year can feel like an opportunity for change.
She accepted an opportunity to work abroad.

vocabulary.meaning: to become better or make something better
examples: He wants to improve his health this year.
Small daily habits can improve your English.

vocabulary.meaning: the reason or energy that makes someone want to do something
examples: Strong motivation makes goals easier to reach.
Her motivation increased after she saw progress.

vocabulary.meaning: to feel pleased and excited about something that is going to happen
examples: I look forward to seeing what the new year brings.
They are looking forward to starting the project.
